title: Strip Stray Null Bytes From Repo Lib Index
description: repo/lib/js/index.ts (~182KB, ~4475 lines, imported by most script.ts files for shared lint/policy/runner utilities) contains 2 raw null bytes (0x00) at byte offsets 47705 and 47752. This makes `file` classify it as "data" instead of text, and makes plain `grep` (without -a) silently return zero matches for anything in the file, even definitely-defined symbols. Locate exact context, confirm the null bytes are inert (inside a string/regex literal used as a glob-to-regex sentinel placeholder in coverageGlobToRegExp, not accidental corruption of surrounding code), replace them with the equivalent textual escape sequence so the file becomes plain ASCII/UTF-8 text with identical runtime behavior, then verify with `file` and a lint/build smoke check.
summary: Found 2 raw NUL bytes (0x00) at byte offsets 47705 and 47752 in repo/lib/js/index.ts, inside coverageGlobToRegExp's glob-to-regex sentinel placeholder (a string literal "\x00" and a regex literal /\x00/). They were literal control-byte characters rather than the textual 4-char escape sequence \x00, which made `file` classify the file as "data" and made plain (non -a) grep silently skip the entire file, returning zero matches even for symbols that are definitely defined (dispatchPolicyArgv, defineLint, etc.). Replaced both raw NUL bytes with the textual \x00 escape sequence, which parses to the exact same runtime string/regex content in JS/TS, so behavior is unchanged. Verified: `file` now reports the file as UTF-8/ASCII text; plain grep finds dispatchPolicyArgv, defineLint, coverageGlobToRegExp; a runtime smoke test via `bun -e` confirmed isCoverageExcluded/coverageGlobToRegExp still work correctly; `bun ./📜️script.ts test quick` passes 88/90 tests (the 2 failures are pre-existing and unrelated — about PLAYGROUND_SITE_HOSTS/playgroundDevPort for "cad"/"dag" kinds tied to concurrent work on framework/plugin/registry/generated/playgrounds.ts, confirmed by git diff showing my change scoped to only lines 1193-1198).
